80	@background_task
81	def case_add_or_reactivate_participant_flow(
82	    user_email: str,
83	    case_id: int,
84	    participant_role: ParticipantRoleType = ParticipantRoleType.observer,
85	    service_id: int = 0,
86	    add_to_conversation: bool = True,
87	    event: dict = None,
88	    organization_slug: str = None,
89	    db_session=None,
90	):
91	    """Runs the case add or reactive participant flow."""
92	    case = case_service.get(db_session=db_session, case_id=case_id)
93	
94	    if service_id:
95	        # we need to ensure that we don't add another member of a service if one
96	        # already exists (e.g. overlapping oncalls, we assume they will hand-off if necessary)
97	        participant = participant_service.get_by_case_id_and_service_id(
98	            case_id=case_id, service_id=service_id, db_session=db_session
99	        )
100	
101	        if participant:
102	            log.debug("Skipping resolved participant. Oncall service member already engaged.")
103	            return
104	
105	    participant = participant_service.get_by_case_id_and_email(
106	        db_session=db_session, case_id=case.id, email=user_email
107	    )
108	    if participant:
109	        if participant.active_roles:
110	            return participant
111	
112	        if case.status != CaseStatus.closed:
113	            # we reactivate the participant
114	            participant_flows.reactivate_participant(
115	                user_email, case, db_session, service_id=service_id
116	            )
117	    else:
118	        # we add the participant to the case
119	        participant = participant_flows.add_participant(
120	            user_email, case, db_session, service_id=service_id, roles=[participant_role]
121	        )
122	    if case.tactical_group:
123	        # we add the participant to the tactical group
124	        group_flows.update_group(
125	            subject=case,
126	            group=case.tactical_group,
127	            group_action=GroupAction.add_member,
128	            group_member=participant.individual.email,
129	            db_session=db_session,
130	        )
131	
132	    if case.status != CaseStatus.closed:
133	        # we add the participant to the conversation
134	        if add_to_conversation:
135	            conversation_flows.add_case_participants(
136	                case, [participant.individual.email], db_session
137	            )
138	
139	            # check to see if there is an override welcome message template
140	            welcome_template = email_template_service.get_by_type(
141	                db_session=db_session,
142	                project_id=case.project_id,
143	                email_template_type=EmailTemplateTypes.case_welcome,
144	            )
145	
146	            send_case_welcome_participant_message(
147	                participant_email=user_email,
148	                case=case,
149	                db_session=db_session,
150	                welcome_template=welcome_template,
151	            )
152	
153	        # Update the participants canvas since a new participant was added
154	        try:
155	            canvas_flows.update_participants_canvas(case=case, db_session=db_session)
156	            log.info(f"Updated participants canvas for case {case.id} after adding {user_email}")
157	        except Exception as e:
158	            log.exception(f"Failed to update participants canvas for case {case.id}: {e}")
159	
160	    return participant
161

The function is `add_case_participants` in `src/dispatch/conversation/flows.py`. It is called from `case_add_or_reactivate_participant_flow` in `src/dispatch/case/flows.py`, which hands off to it when a person is added to a case. I did not change any code.

**Hand-opened cases:** No. The thread branch only runs when `case.signal_instances` is non-empty. A case opened by hand has no signal instances, so nobody is added to its thread.

**Alert-raised cases:** The alert's signal definition must have `lifecycle` set to `"production"`. The check reads `case.signal_instances[0].signal.lifecycle` and only calls `plugin.instance.add_to_thread(...)` when it equals `"production"`. The `lifecycle` column is defined on the signal model in `src/dispatch/signal/models.py`. Other lifecycle values are not added to the thread.

Two conditions also apply: the case must have a thread (`has_thread`, which means a conversation with a `thread_id`), and the case must not be closed.
